# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 3
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👊 ✊ 👍 ✊]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 👉 ✊]

Now I have two gestures.

Mute: ✋ 👊 ✊ 👍 ✊ — five symbols. This is presumably the manual's instruction for the current state (green light, display 0, wires 1 green 2 red 3 blue).

Blind: 👋 👉 ✊ — three symbols. Blind can't see, so Blind gesturing is odd — wait, Blind can't see, but can Blind gesture? The table says Blind can reach the bomb, cannot see. Gestures are made with hands. Blind could make gestures but wouldn't know what they're signing? Actually the rules don't forbid Blind gesturing. But Blind receives gestures? "Whoever can see receives it." Blind cannot see, so Blind receives a blank per symbol. So Blind wouldn't know what I gesture. But Blind CAN gesture, and I can see it.

Hmm, but Blind gesturing 👋 👉 ✊ — Blind can't see, so how would Blind know these symbols? Unless Blind is just making hand shapes blindly. Actually, maybe Blind is trying to communicate. But Blind has no manual and can't see. Blind's gesture is strange.

Wait — reconsider. Blind can hear speech. So I can speak to Blind. Blind gesturing to me is a channel Blind has: Blind makes gestures, I see them. But Blind can't see my gestures back. So Blind→Deaf gesture is one-way useful.

Blind's gesture 👋 👉 ✊: "wave, point, fist" — could mean "go ahead" or "point to wire 3"? 👉 could mean "that one", ✊ could mean wire... unclear.

Actually, let me reconsider the whole situation. Let me focus on what matters: I need to tell Blind which wire to cut. I speak to Blind (Blind hears). Mute hears too.

Mute's latest gesture ✋ 👊 ✊ 👍 ✊ is the instruction. But I can't decode it. However — maybe the gestures ARE the code and I'm overcomplicating. The manual presumably uses the gesture alphabet as a code. Mute reads the manual and translates into gestures for me. But I can't read the manual, so I can't decode gestures either. That's the crux: Mute must communicate the instruction in a way I can act on.

Hmm, but I can't act. Blind acts. So the chain is: Mute reads manual → tells me (via gesture or speech) → I tell Blind (via speech) → Blind cuts wire.

Wait, Mute can speak? No — Mute cannot speak. Mute can read the manual and gesture. Deaf can see gestures. So Mute gestures to Deaf, Deaf speaks to Blind. That's the chain.

So Mute's gesture ✋ 👊 ✊ 👍 ✊ must encode "cut wire N". I need to interpret it. But I can't read the manual... The gesture symbols might map to something. Actually maybe the manual literally says "the correct wire is the one whose... " and Mute encodes the wire number.

Let me think about the symbols as possibly encoding numbers or positions. ✋ (open hand, 5 fingers), 👊 (fist, 0), ✊ (fist), 👍 (thumbs up), ✊.

Hmm. Alternatively, maybe the number of symbols or a specific symbol indicates the wire. The first gesture was 9 symbols, second 4, third 5. Not obviously wire numbers (1,2,3).

Actually — maybe I'm wrong that I can't decode. The manual is Mute's. Mute translates. The translation scheme must be something we can agree on without a shared code... but we have no prior agreement. Unless the manual itself defines a gesture code, and Mute expects me to know it? I don't have the manual.

Let me reconsider: perhaps the gestures aren't a code at all, but Mute is spelling out letters using the gesture alphabet as a sign-language alphabet. But the symbols given are emoji hands, not letters.

Given the ambiguity, the safest path: I should ask Mute to communicate the wire number in a way I can understand — e.g., by speaking... no, Mute can't speak. Hmm.

Wait, actually — can Mute speak? "Mute: Read the manual. Cannot: Speak, or touch the bomb." So Mute cannot speak. Mute can only gesture. And only Deaf sees gestures. So Mute→Deaf gesture is the only Mute output.

And Deaf→(Mute, Blind) speech. Deaf→Mute gesture.

So the only way Mute conveys the wire is via gestures to me. I must interpret. Since I can't read the manual, the gesture must be self-describing or use a convention.

Maybe the convention: Mute gestures the wire number as a count, or points. Let me look: ✋ 👊 ✊ 👍 ✊. Hmm, 👍 is "thumbs up" = good/correct. Maybe 👍 marks the correct wire, and the position of 👍 in the sequence indicates which wire. 👍 is the 4th symbol. That doesn't map to 1-3.

Alternatively, maybe the symbols before/after 👍 encode the wire. Or the number of ✊ (fist) symbols = wire number? ✊ appears 3 times in ✋ 👊 ✊ 👍 ✊? No: ✊ appears twice (positions 3 and 5). 👊 once. Hmm.

Let me count in the first gesture: ✊ ✋ 👊 ✊ ✋ 👊 ✊ 👊 ✋ — ✊ appears 4 times? positions 1,4,7,9? Let me recount: ✊(1) ✋(2) 👊(3) ✊(4) ✋(5) 👊(6) ✊(7) 👊(8) ✋(9). ✊ at 1,4,7 = 3 times. ✋ at 2,5,9 = 3 times. 👊 at 3,6,8 = 3 times. Interesting — 3 each! That's a pattern: three groups.

Second gesture: ✋ 👊 ✊ ✊ — ✋ once, 👊 once, ✊ twice.

Third: ✋ 👊 ✊ 👍 ✊ — ✋ once, 👊 once, ✊ twice, 👍 once.

Hmm, the first gesture had a clean 3-3-3 pattern. Maybe it was a calibration/handshake.

This is getting speculative. Let me step back and consider the practical move. Blind is asking me something (👋 👉 ✊ — "wave, point, fist"). Blind might be asking "which one do I point at / grab?" I should respond to Blind.

But I don't yet have a confident wire. However, maybe I should just relay Mute's instruction and trust the chain. But I can't decode it, so I can't relay a wire number.

Alternative: Maybe the intended reading is simpler than I think. Perhaps Mute's gesture directly encodes the wire via the gesture alphabet's ordering, and I'm supposed to recognize... no.

Let me reconsider the roles. Actually, re-read: "A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never read it out." This suggests some markings can't be named. The gesture alphabet is the "alphabet below" — symbols. Speech "carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation, and nothing else." So gestures carry symbols, speech carries words/numbers.

So Mute, who reads the manual, might need to convey a symbol (a marking on the bomb) — but Mute can't see the bomb! So Mute can't know the bomb's markings. Only Deaf sees markings. So Deaf describes markings to Mute via speech (words/numbers). Mute matches to manual.

So: I describe the bomb (colors, display, wires) in words. Mute reads manual, finds the matching entry, and must tell me the action. The action might be "cut wire X" where X is a number — Mute can gesture a number? But gestures are symbols, not numbers. Hmm, but Mute could gesture a symbol that represents the wire.

Actually wait — maybe Mute CAN convey numbers, because Mute gestures to Deaf, and Deaf then speaks numbers to Blind. The gesture alphabet might encode numbers by finger count! ✋ = 5, ☝ = 1, ✌ = 2, 🤟 = 3? No... Let me think: ✌ is two fingers (2), ☝ is one finger (1), 🤟 is "I love you" (3 fingers extended?), ✊ is fist (0), ✋ is open hand (5).

So finger-count gestures could be numbers! ✊=0, ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3 (index+pinky+thumb = 3?), ✋=5, 👊=fist=0.

Mute's gesture ✋ 👊 ✊ 👍 ✊: ✋=5, 👊=0, ✊=0, 👍=?, ✊=0. Hmm, "500?0"? Not clean.

Maybe it's not finger-count.

I think I'm overanalyzing without enough info. Let me just do the sensible thing: respond to Blind, and ask Mute for a clearer signal. Actually, better: I should tell Mute the current full state again and ask Mute to give the wire number in an unambiguous way, and I'll relay to Blind.

But repeated back-and-forth wastes turns and the bomb is armed. Let me be decisive but safe.

Hmm, actually, let me reconsider: maybe the gesture sequences ARE the manual's instructions and the game expects me to just relay them to Blind by describing... no, Blind can't see gestures.

Wait — here's a key insight: Blind can HEAR my speech. So I speak the wire number to Blind. To get the wire number, I need to decode Mute's gesture. Since I can't read the manual, the only way is if the gesture is self-explanatory (e.g., finger count = wire number).

Let me look for a finger-count in Mute's latest: ✋ 👊 ✊ 👍 ✊. If I count extended fingers: ✋=5, 👊=0, ✊=0, 👍=1 (thumb), ✊=0. Sum=6? No.

Maybe the relevant symbol is 👍 (thumbs up = "this one is good") and its position among wire-like symbols. Or maybe Mute is indicating "wire 3" because... hmm.

Alternatively, maybe the sequence ✋ 👊 ✊ 👍 ✊ is a repeat/confirmation and the actual answer is elsewhere.

I think the honest move: I cannot decode the manual's code, and I should say so and ask Mute to encode the wire as a finger-count gesture (1, 2, or 3 fingers) which is self-evident. Let me propose that convention explicitly so Mute can use it.

Also respond to Blind: acknowledge, say I'm getting the wire number.

Let me write:

speak(to="mute", text="I cannot read the manual, so I cannot decode your gesture code. Please tell me the wire number using finger count: one finger for wire 1, two for wire 2, three for wire 3. Current state: display 0, light green, wires 1 green 2 red 3 blue.")

speak(to="blind", text="Hold on. I see display 0, light green, wires 1 green 2 red 3 blue. Waiting for the wire number from Mute, then I will tell you which wire to cut.")

gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝"]) — hmm, that might confuse. Maybe gesture to Mute the finger-count convention: ☝ ✌ 🤟? That shows 1,2,3. Let me gesture ["☝","✌","🤟"] to establish the convention.

Actually gesturing to Mute is fine (Mute sees). Let me do that.

Let me finalize.

Actually, wait. Let me reconsider whether Mute might already be using finger-count and I should read it. ✋ 👊 ✊ 👍 ✊ — no clean count. So probably not. My proposal stands.

Let me also consider: is it possible the bomb state is such that the answer is obvious? Display 0, green light. Common bomb-defusal trope: if display is 0 and light is green, cut... unknown. No.

I'll go with asking for finger-count and informing Blind.

One more: Blind gestured 👋 👉 ✊. 👋 = wave (hello), 👉 = point, ✊ = fist. Maybe Blind is saying "hello, I'll grab (fist) the one you point to." So Blind is ready. Good — I just need the wire.

Final answer.Two gestures arrived. Mute's ✋ 👊 ✊ 👍 ✊ is presumably the manual's instruction, but I can't read the manual, so I can't decode Mute's gesture code — I have no shared key for it. Blind's 👋 👉 ✊ looks like "hello, I'll grab the one you point to," so Blind is ready and waiting on me.

The critical problem: I must turn Mute's instruction into a wire number I can speak to Blind. Since I can't decode an arbitrary gesture code, I need Mute to use a self-evident encoding — finger count. I'll propose that convention explicitly, re-state the current bomb state so Mute is working from the right light (it changed yellow→green), and tell Blind to stand by.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot read the manual, so I cannot decode your gesture code. Please give me the wire number by finger count: one finger for wire 1, two fingers for wire 2, three fingers for wire 3. Current state: display 0, light green, wires 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue.")
speak(to="blind", text="Stand by. I see display 0, light green, wires 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. I am getting the wire number from Mute, then I will tell you exactly which wire to cut.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 4
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌]

The light went back from green to yellow. Display still 0. Wires unchanged.

Mute now gestures a single symbol: 🤟. In my proposed convention, 🤟 was my "three" gesture (index, pinky, thumb extended). But wait — I proposed ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3. Mute responded with 🤟 = three fingers = wire 3. That fits my convention exactly. Mute is telling me: cut wire 3.

Blind gestures 👌 = "OK" — Blind is ready/acknowledging.

But caution: the light changed again (green→yellow). Does the wire answer depend on the light? Mute's earlier gestures came in under yellow (turn 1), then green (turn 2,3), now yellow again (turn 4). The current state is yellow, display 0, wires 1 green 2 red 3 blue. Mute's latest single gesture 🤟 was sent in response to my finger-count request, which I made while describing the green-light state. Hmm — I described green in my last message, but the light is now yellow.

This is a real risk. Mute may have answered for green, but the bomb now shows yellow. However, the light seems to be toggling on its own (yellow→green→yellow), possibly a blinking indicator rather than a state that changes the answer. Or it genuinely changes the correct wire.

Given the ambiguity, I should confirm with Mute that wire 3 is correct for the CURRENT state (yellow, display 0). But I also don't want to stall forever. Let me relay to Blind the tentative answer (wire 3) but flag the light change and ask Mute to confirm. Actually — Blind acts; a wrong action detonates. I must not give Blind a wrong wire.

Best: tell Mute the light is now yellow again and ask to confirm wire 3 still holds. Tell Blind to hold. Then next turn, if Mute confirms, I give Blind the go.

But turns are limited and the bomb is armed — I don't know how many turns remain. Still, safety first: one confirmation is worth it.

Actually, let me reconsider. The light toggling yellow↔green each turn might just be the bomb's normal behavior (a blinking light), not a state change. The display stays 0, wires stay same. So the "state" is essentially stable and the light is just blinking. In that case Mute's 🤟 = wire 3 is the answer.

Hmm, but I explicitly told Mute "light green" in my last message, and the light is now yellow. If Mute's manual keys off the light color, Mute answered for green. Risk.

I'll do a quick confirm but also give Blind a conditional. Actually Blind can't do conditionals usefully — Blind just cuts. Let me confirm with Mute and hold Blind.

Let me also gesture back 🤟 to Mute to confirm I read "three," and ask if it's for yellow.

Decision: 
- speak to Mute: light is yellow again now; confirm 🤟 (wire 3) is correct for yellow, display 0.
- speak to Blind: hold, nearly there.
- gesture to Mute: 🤟 (acknowledge three).

Hmm, but if I keep holding Blind and Mute keeps answering, we might loop. Let me make this the confirmation turn and be ready to commit next.

Actually, you know, let me reconsider the risk of the light. The problem statement says "every reading it gives" — the light is a reading. It changed. Could be meaningful. I'll confirm.

Let me write it.Mute answered with a single 🤟 — in the finger-count convention I proposed, that's three fingers = wire 3. Blind's 👌 confirms readiness. But the light has flipped back to yellow (it was green when I asked). If the manual keys off the light, Mute may have answered for green, not the current yellow. I can't risk a wrong wire, so I'll confirm with Mute and keep Blind holding.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I read your 🤟 as three fingers = wire 3. But the light has changed again: it is now yellow, display still 0, wires 1 green 2 red 3 blue. Confirm: is wire 3 correct for the yellow light, display 0? If yes, gesture 🤟 again.")
speak(to="blind", text="Almost there. Hold. I have a candidate wire but the light just changed, so I am confirming with Mute before you cut.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤟"])
```

(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is

LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌 ✊]

Light is green again. Display 0. Wires unchanged.

Mute re-sent 🤟 = three = wire 3. That's a confirmation, and it's the same answer regardless of the light toggling (Mute gave 🤟 under green before, and now under green again — consistent). The light appears to just be blinking yellow↔green; the answer is stable: wire 3.

Blind gestures 👌 ✊ = "OK, fist" = "OK, I'll grab/cut." Blind is ready and waiting for my go.

I'm now confident enough: display 0, wires 1 green 2 red 3 blue, cut wire 3 (blue). Mute confirmed twice with 🤟. I'll tell Blind to cut wire 3.

I should give Blind a clear, unambiguous instruction: cut wire 3, the blue one.

Let me also acknowledge Mute.

speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 3. That is the blue wire. Cut wire 3 now.")
speak(to="mute", text="Confirmed: wire 3. I am telling Blind to cut wire 3, the blue one.")

I'm confident now: cut wire 3, the blue one. I'll give Blind the explicit instruction and acknowledge Mute.

speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 3. That is the blue wire. Cut wire 3 now.")
speak(to="mute", text="Confirmed: wire 3. I am telling Blind to cut wire 3, the blue one.")
